name: Unprotected initialize() on an unverified BSC swap router
summary: The unverified swap contract's initialize() had no access control and had never been called, so its owner was still zero. The attacker's contract called initialize() to become owner and then withdrawFees(address,uint256) to take the contract's 23 BNB.
notes: owner() was zero until the anchor, whose own initialize() call is the earliest one (rule 10). The only storage change before it, slot 0 going from 0 to 1 in an ordinary user swap (0x9352bdee), left owner() at zero and is not a reset. Later initialize() and withdrawFees() calls by others reverted, and the creator's sibling deployments never paid out BNB.
